controls.control_description: Conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information held by the covered entity.
controls.typical_evidence: Risk assessment report, asset inventory, threat catalog, vulnerability scan results
controls.pharmacy_context: Annual risk analysis covering pharmacy management system, patient prescription database, insurance interfaces, and workstation endpoints

controls.control_description: Implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level to comply with § 164.306(a).
controls.typical_evidence: Risk treatment plan, mitigation implementation records, residual risk acceptance documentation
controls.pharmacy_context: Documented remediation of identified pharmacy system risks (e.g., unencrypted backup drives, shared workstation credentials)

controls.control_description: Apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with the security policies and procedures.
controls.typical_evidence: Employee handbook section, documented disciplinary actions for security violations
controls.pharmacy_context: Policy stating consequences for snooping on celebrity patient profiles or sharing pharmacy system passwords

controls.control_description: Implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports.
controls.typical_evidence: Log review schedule, audit log samples, review sign-off records
controls.pharmacy_context: Weekly review of pharmacy system audit logs for unusual prescription access patterns or after-hours logins

controls.control_description: Identify the security official who is responsible for the development and implementation of the policies and procedures required by this subpart for the entity.
controls.typical_evidence: Job description, appointment memo, security responsibilities document
controls.pharmacy_context: Designated pharmacy compliance officer or IT security coordinator with documented HIPAA security duties

controls.control_description: Implement procedures for the authorization and/or supervision of workforce members who work with electronic protected health information or in locations where it might be accessed.
controls.typical_evidence: Role-based access matrix, supervisor approval workflow for new hires accessing PHI systems
controls.pharmacy_context: Pharmacy manager approves new technician's access to the dispensing system before account provisioning

controls.control_description: Implement procedures to determine that the access of a workforce member to electronic protected health information is appropriate.
controls.typical_evidence: Background check policy, access justification forms, periodic access recertification
controls.pharmacy_context: Annual re-certification that each pharmacy staff member still needs their current level of PHI system access

controls.control_description: Implement procedures for terminating access to electronic protected health information when the employment of, or other arrangement with, a workforce member ends or as required by determinations made as per access authorization.
controls.typical_evidence: Offboarding checklist, IT deprovisioning tickets, badge return log
controls.pharmacy_context: Same-day deactivation of pharmacy system accounts and alarm codes when a technician is terminated

controls.control_description: If a health care clearinghouse is part of a larger organization, the clearinghouse must implement policies and procedures that protect the electronic protected health information of the clearinghouse from unauthorized access by the larger organization.
controls.typical_evidence: Network segmentation documentation, firewall rules, access control policies separating clearinghouse from parent org
controls.pharmacy_context: If pharmacy uses a clearinghouse for claims processing, clearinghouse PHI is firewalled from retail store operations

controls.control_description: Implement policies and procedures for granting access to electronic protected health information, for example through access to a workstation, transaction, program, process, or other mechanism.
controls.typical_evidence: Access request forms, role-based access control (RBAC) matrix, manager approval workflow
controls.pharmacy_context: Technicians get dispensing system access; cashiers do not. Manager must approve all access requests.

controls.control_description: Implement policies and procedures that, based upon the entity's access authorization policies, establish, document, review, and modify a user's right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process.
controls.typical_evidence: User provisioning procedure, access modification log, quarterly access review documentation
controls.pharmacy_context: When a technician is promoted to lead, their access is modified via ticket and documented; old access is revoked

controls.control_description: Periodic security updates and reminders about malicious software protection, log-in monitoring, and password management.
controls.typical_evidence: Phishing simulation reports, security newsletter records, training completion certificates
controls.pharmacy_context: Monthly pharmacy team email reminding staff not to click suspicious links and to verify sender addresses

controls.control_description: Procedures for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software.
controls.typical_evidence: Antivirus deployment records, email filtering logs, incident response procedures for malware
controls.pharmacy_context: Pharmacy workstations run endpoint protection with automatic updates; USB ports disabled on patient-facing terminals

controls.control_description: Procedures for monitoring log-in attempts and reporting discrepancies.
controls.typical_evidence: SIEM alerts for failed logins, account lockout policy, anomaly detection rules
controls.pharmacy_context: Alert when pharmacy system sees 5 failed logins in 10 minutes or logins outside operating hours

controls.control_description: Procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords.
controls.typical_evidence: Password policy (length, complexity, rotation), technical enforcement (AD/LDAP group policy), password manager use
controls.pharmacy_context: Pharmacy system enforces 12-character minimum, no shared accounts, password manager for admin credentials

controls.control_description: Identify and respond to suspected or known security incidents; mitigate, to the extent practicable, harmful effects of security incidents that are known to the covered entity; and document security incidents and their outcomes.
controls.typical_evidence: Incident response plan, incident log, post-incident review documentation, escalation contact list
controls.pharmacy_context: Documented procedure for reporting suspected breach (unauthorized PHI viewing, lost laptop with patient data) to compliance officer within 1 hour

controls.control_description: Establish and implement procedures to create and maintain retrievable exact copies of electronic protected health information.
controls.typical_evidence: Backup schedule, backup restoration test records, offsite/cloud backup configuration
controls.pharmacy_context: Daily encrypted backup of pharmacy management system to cloud with quarterly restoration drill

controls.control_description: Establish and implement procedures to restore any loss of data.
controls.typical_evidence: DR plan with RTO/RPO targets, failover procedures, annual DR test results
controls.pharmacy_context: If primary pharmacy server fails, failover to redundant system within 4 hours; tested annually

controls.control_description: Establish and implement procedures to enable continuation of critical business processes for protection of the security of electronic protected health information while operating in emergency mode.
controls.typical_evidence: Emergency operations procedure, paper fallback workflow, contact tree for emergency activation
controls.pharmacy_context: If network is down, pharmacy can operate on paper prescriptions for up to 24 hours with documented manual PHI protection

controls.control_description: Implement procedures for periodic testing and revision of contingency plans.
controls.typical_evidence: Annual DR test report, tabletop exercise minutes, plan revision log
controls.pharmacy_context: Annual disaster recovery tabletop exercise with pharmacy staff; plan updated based on findings

controls.control_description: Assess the relative criticality of specific applications and data in support of other contingency plan components.
controls.typical_evidence: Criticality matrix ranking systems by business impact, data classification inventory
controls.pharmacy_context: Pharmacy management system ranked Tier 1 (dispense prescriptions); marketing email list ranked Tier 3

controls.control_description: Perform a periodic technical and non-technical evaluation of the security policies and procedures that demonstrate and document compliance with the standards and implementation specifications.
controls.typical_evidence: Annual security evaluation report, penetration test results, policy review minutes
controls.pharmacy_context: Annual third-party security assessment of pharmacy systems and review of all administrative safeguard policies

controls.control_description: Implement policies and procedures to safeguard the facility and the equipment therein from unauthorized physical access, tampering, and theft.
controls.typical_evidence: Facility security plan, badge access logs, visitor escort policy, camera coverage map
controls.pharmacy_context: Pharmacy back room (where servers and hard-copy prescriptions are stored) requires badge access; visitors escorted

controls.control_description: Implement procedures to control and validate a person's access to facilities based on their role or function, including visitor control, and control of access to software testing and revision.
controls.typical_evidence: Role-based badge access levels, visitor log, sign-in/sign-out procedure
controls.pharmacy_context: Technicians can badge into pharmacy; delivery drivers must sign in and be escorted

controls.control_description: Implement procedures to document repairs and modifications to the physical components of a facility which are related to security (e.g., hardware, walls, doors, and locks).
controls.typical_evidence: Maintenance log for security hardware, work order records for door/lock repairs
controls.pharmacy_context: Log of all locksmith work, door repairs, and alarm system maintenance with before/after photos

controls.control_description: Implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic protected health information.
controls.typical_evidence: Workstation use policy, screen privacy filter deployment, workstation positioning standards
controls.pharmacy_context: Patient-facing pharmacy terminals positioned so screens are not visible to waiting customers; privacy filters on all displays

controls.control_description: Implement physical safeguards for all workstations that access electronic protected health information, to restrict access to authorized users.
controls.typical_evidence: Cable locks, locked offices, auto-locking screen savers, clean desk policy
controls.pharmacy_context: All pharmacy workstations have cable locks; screens lock after 5 minutes of inactivity; no PHI left on printers

controls.control_description: Implement policies and procedures to address the final disposition of electronic protected health information, and/or the hardware or electronic media on which it is stored.
controls.typical_evidence: Media disposal procedure, certificate of destruction from vendor, degaussing/shredding records
controls.pharmacy_context: Old pharmacy hard drives sent to certified e-waste vendor with documented chain of custody and certificate of destruction

controls.control_description: Implement procedures for removal of electronic protected health information from electronic media before the media are made available for re-use.
controls.typical_evidence: Media sanitization procedure, wipe verification logs, re-use approval workflow
controls.pharmacy_context: USB drives and external disks must be cryptographically wiped (not just formatted) before re-use in non-PHI contexts

controls.control_description: Maintain a record of the movements of hardware and electronic media and any person responsible therefore.
controls.typical_evidence: Hardware asset inventory, media tracking log, checkout/check-in procedure
controls.pharmacy_context: All pharmacy laptops and backup tapes are tracked in asset inventory; checked out to named individuals only

controls.control_description: Create a retrievable, exact copy of electronic protected health information, when needed, before movement of equipment.
controls.typical_evidence: Pre-move backup procedure, verification that backup is restorable before equipment relocation
controls.pharmacy_context: Before moving the pharmacy server to a new location, full backup is taken and restoration is verified

controls.control_description: Assign a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity.
controls.typical_evidence: No shared accounts policy, user ID naming convention, account provisioning procedure
controls.pharmacy_context: Every pharmacy staff member has their own login; no 'pharmacy1' or 'frontdesk' shared accounts permitted

controls.control_description: Establish and implement procedures for obtaining necessary electronic protected health information during an emergency.
controls.typical_evidence: Break-glass procedure, emergency access log, post-emergency access review
controls.pharmacy_context: Emergency break-glass account for accessing pharmacy system during system admin absence; usage is logged and reviewed within 24 hours

controls.control_description: Implement electronic procedures that terminate an electronic session after a predetermined time of inactivity.
controls.typical_evidence: Group policy / application settings showing session timeout configuration (e.g., 15 minutes)
controls.pharmacy_context: Pharmacy management system logs out users after 10 minutes of inactivity; screen locks after 5 minutes at OS level

controls.control_description: Implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information.
controls.typical_evidence: Encryption at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+), key management documentation, certificate inventory
controls.pharmacy_context: Patient prescription database encrypted at rest; all data transmission between pharmacy and insurer uses TLS 1.3

controls.control_description: Implement hardware, software, and/or procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems that contain or use electronic protected health information.
controls.typical_evidence: Audit log configuration, log retention policy, SIEM or log aggregation setup
controls.pharmacy_context: Pharmacy system logs every prescription view, refill, and insurance query with timestamp, user ID, and patient record ID

controls.control_description: Implement electronic mechanisms to corroborate that electronic protected health information has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.
controls.typical_evidence: File integrity monitoring (FIM), checksum/hashing for critical files, database integrity constraints
controls.pharmacy_context: File integrity monitoring on pharmacy server configuration files; database transaction logs for audit trail

controls.control_description: Implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic protected health information is the one claimed.
controls.typical_evidence: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) deployment, password policy enforcement, biometric or smart card access
controls.pharmacy_context: Pharmacy system requires username/password plus hardware token or SMS OTP for remote access; biometric for local admin

controls.control_description: Implement security measures to ensure that electronically transmitted electronic protected health information is not improperly modified without detection until disposed of.
controls.typical_evidence: TLS with HMAC, message signing for API integrations, VPN tunneling for remote transmission
controls.pharmacy_context: All HL7/FHIR messages between pharmacy and health system use signed payloads; VPN required for remote pharmacy access

controls.control_description: Implement a mechanism to encrypt electronic protected health information whenever deemed appropriate.
controls.typical_evidence: TLS 1.2+ for all external transmission, IPsec for site-to-site, encrypted email gateway
controls.pharmacy_context: Email containing PHI sent through encrypted gateway; fax uses encrypted transmission; no unencrypted PHI over public internet
